items.name: Amount
items.tip: Amount: 0 = no ducking at all. Low settings carve only the bands where the sidechain is loud (transparent space). Towards 100 it turns into a full-on pump that ducks everything with each hit. Gradual in between.

items.name: Low cut
items.tip: Low cut: sidechain content below this frequency does not trigger any ducking (stops a kick from carving the whole mix, for example).

items.name: High cut
items.tip: High cut: sidechain content above this frequency does not trigger any ducking.

items.name: Max cut
items.tip: Max cut: the deepest reduction any band can get at 100 % amount.

items.name: Floor
items.tip: Floor: how far below the loudest sidechain band a band can be and still cause ducking. Lower = only the strongest bands duck, higher = more bands duck.

items.name: Drive
items.tip: Drive (PurrOne opamp tanh). Colour: sound dirties the audio you hear with automatic gain staging so it never gets quieter. Colour: sidechain colours what the ducker listens to: more harmonics means more bands duck, so the cut gets wider.

items.name: Transistor
items.tip: Transistor (PurrOne, asymmetric, even harmonics). On the sound: warm, thick even harmonics with the level kept. On the sidechain: the ducker also reacts one octave up from the fundamental.

items.name: Fuzz
items.tip: Fuzz (PurrOne lopsided clip with octave-up growl). On the sound: nasty fuzz with the level kept. On the sidechain: spreads the sidechain energy across the spectrum, so a bass or kick carves holes far up (and the result gets quieter).

items.name: Colour
items.tip: Where Drive, Transistor and Fuzz act. Sound: dirties the audio you hear, level kept. Sidechain: only colours what the ducker listens to (Audition shows it). Both: does both. Not ducked: colours only what the sidechain never touches, below the Low cut and above the High cut (needs those set inside 20 Hz to 20 kHz).

items.name: Freeze
items.tip: Freeze: holds the current sidechain curve so it keeps carving the same gaps (a static EQ taken from the sidechain).

items.name: Audition
items.tip: Audition: listen to the sidechain as the plugin hears it (after low and high cut). Useful for setting the cuts.

items.name: Attack
items.tip: Attack: how fast the ducking engages when the sidechain gets loud.

items.name: Release
items.tip: Release: how long the ducking takes to let go after the sidechain stops. Short = tight, long = the big breathing pump.

items.name: Latency
items.tip: Latency: the delay this plugin adds (the host compensates). Ultra 256 is about 6 ms, Low 512 about 11 ms, Normal 1024 about 21 ms, High 2048 about 43 ms. Shorter = tighter timing but less precise at low frequencies; longer = cleaner and more exact in the bass.

items.name: Pan
items.tip: Pan: moves the effect toward one side. Left of centre applies less to the right channel, right of centre applies less to the left (or to side instead of mid in M/S).

items.name: Mix
items.tip: Mix: dry/wet blend of the ducked signal.

items.name: Stereo mode
items.tip: Stereo mode: L/R ducks left and right, M/S ducks mid and side.

top.name: Preset menu
top.tip: Factory presets (our own). Use the arrows to step through them.

top.name: Randomize
top.tip: Set the controls to random values (output level and on/off switches are kept).

top.name: Nasty range
top.tip: Nasty range: lets Drive, Fuzz, Squeeze, Warm and the other heavy knobs go far past 100 % for really nasty, OTT and Vengeance style sounds. Off keeps every knob at its normal top.

top.name: Limiter
top.tip: Safety limiter on the output: keeps the level from ever passing 0 dBFS, smooth and transparent. Turn it off if you want the raw output (for example to let your own limiter do the work).

top.name: Settings
top.tip: Settings: version, link to the GitHub page for new versions

top.name: Info bubbles (i)
top.tip: Info bubbles: hover a control for one second to see what it does. Click to turn them off or on.
